steps: Using SI units provides a common, internationally accepted system of measurement.
Standard units prevent confusion and errors when measurements are recorded, communicated, or used in calculations.
Accurate and consistent measurements help people make reliable decisions and avoid accidents, especially in science, engineering, and medicine.
items.finalAnswer: SI units provide standard, clear measurements that reduce confusion and errors, making results more reliable and helping ensure safety.

steps: Yes. A measurement can be both inaccurate and imprecise.
It is inaccurate when it is far from the true value.
It is imprecise when repeated measurements differ greatly from one another.
items.finalAnswer: Yes; measurements may be far from the true value and also vary greatly when repeated.

steps: Space exploration involves scientists and engineers in different countries working together.
Using the same SI units allows them to communicate measurements and use data consistently.
Consistent units are essential for calculations involving spacecraft, distances, speeds, masses, and forces.
Using SI units helps prevent conversion mistakes that could cause a spacecraft to follow the wrong path or a mission to fail.
items.finalAnswer: SI units provide a common measurement system for space missions, enabling consistent calculations and communication while reducing dangerous errors.
